title: Philippians Bible Quiz - Chapter 4
description: Ten questions on Philippians 4: rejoicing and prayer instead of anxiety, what to think about, and the gift sent from Philippi.

questions.text: Which two women does the writer exhort to think the same way in the Lord?
questions.explanation: Verse 2 says "I exhort Euodia, and I exhort Syntyche, to think the same way in the Lord."

answers.text: Lydia and Phoebe
Mary and Martha
Euodia and Syntyche
Priscilla and Claudia

questions.text: Where does verse 3 say the names of his fellow workers are?
questions.explanation: Verse 3 asks his true partner to help these women, who labored with him in the Good News with Clement and the rest of his fellow workers, whose names are in the book of life.

answers.text: In the book of life
On a letter sent to Macedonia
Among the overseers at Philippi
In the records of Caesar's household

questions.text: What are they to let be known to all men?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 says "Let your gentleness be known to all men. The Lord is at hand."

answers.text: Their learning
Their generosity
Their sufferings
Their gentleness

questions.text: Instead of being anxious, what does verse 6 tell them to do?
questions.explanation: Verse 6 says that in nothing they should be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, their requests should be made known to God.

answers.text: Wait quietly until the Lord comes, who is at hand
Make their requests known to God by prayer and petition with thanksgiving
Ask the elders of the assembly to decide for them
Keep their needs to themselves and say nothing

questions.text: What will the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, do?
questions.explanation: Verse 7 says the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard their hearts and their thoughts in Christ Jesus.

answers.text: Silence every adversary around them
Open a door for the word they speak
Guard their hearts and their thoughts in Christ Jesus
Remove all affliction from them

questions.text: What kinds of things does verse 8 tell them to think about?
questions.explanation: Verse 8 lists whatever things are true, honorable, just, pure, lovely and of good report, and tells them to think about these things.

answers.text: Whatever things are old, tested and handed down
Whatever things are hidden, deep and hard to say
Whatever things are useful, strong and lasting
Whatever is true, honorable, just, pure, lovely and of good report

questions.text: What does he say he has learned, in whatever state he is?
questions.explanation: Verses 11 and 12 say he has learned to be content in whatever state he is, knowing both how to be humbled and how to abound, both to be filled and to be hungry.

answers.text: To give thanks for it in the assembly
To be content in it
To say nothing about it to anyone
To ask the Lord to change it

questions.text: What does verse 13 say he can do, and through whom?
questions.explanation: Verse 13 says "I can do all things through Christ, who strengthens me."

answers.text: He can do all things through Christ, who strengthens him
He can bear all things through the prayers of the saints
He can endure all things through the hope laid up for him
He can finish all things through the help sent to him

questions.text: In which city does verse 16 say they sent to his need once and again?
questions.explanation: Verse 16 says "For even in Thessalonica you sent once and again to my need."

answers.text: Laodicea
Colossae
Thessalonica
Ephesus

questions.text: Which saints are singled out in the greetings at the end of the chapter?
questions.explanation: Verse 22 says all the saints greet them, especially those who are of Caesar's household.

answers.text: Those of the house of Clement
Those of Caesar's household
Those who are of the circumcision
Those who travelled from Macedonia
